statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band on a compressed, two-way overnight tape with no observed one-way structure, while stress stays high on the unresolved Gulf war, collapsed Strait of Hormuz traffic and firm crude.
recommendation: Overnight conditions remain consistent with a mean-reverting regime: NQ futures are grinding modestly higher inside a band only about 0.30% wide, with retracements present and no repeated extension observed, while easing yields and fading September hike odds provide a supportive rates backdrop. The mapped policy state is EA_ON, with a narrow danger window flagged around the US cash open and its first hour, where opening-auction structure is resolved.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a 0.3% gain in a tight, holiday-thinned Asian session as Asia firms, September Fed hike odds fall toward 30% and stalled Iran talks keep crude near $88.70 Brent
body: NQ futures trade near 30,241.75, about 0.33% above the 30,141.75 prior settlement, inside an overnight band of roughly 30,163.75-30,255.00 - a range of only about 0.30% - after opening the session near 30,170. Price sits in the upper half of that band, but the band is narrow, retracements are present, and no persistent directional efficiency, failed-retracement sequence or repeated extension has been observed. S&P 500 futures are up about 0.11% and Dow futures are down about 0.12%, a split rather than a trending configuration. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Friday at 30,046.14, down 0.13% inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 range, against a 30,762.20 52-week high, with the VIX at 14.25 near 2026 lows. Asian trade has firmed through the session: Hang Seng is up about 1.6%, Chinese blue chips 0.8%, MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan 0.5% and the Nikkei 0.3%, while South Korea is closed for a public holiday, keeping regional liquidity thin. The Gulf war remains the dominant stress channel and is unresolved. Peace talks have made no progress, Strait of Hormuz transits remain collapsed against roughly 130 vessels a day before the conflict, Iran has publicly linked reopening to sanctions relief and reparations, and Israeli strikes killed at least 11 people in southern Lebanon over the weekend. Crude is holding last week's gains without extending them: Brent is near $88.67, up about 0.2% after a 6% weekly rise, and WTI near $82.19, down about 0.2% after gaining 5.4%. Rates point the other way and are supportive: the 2-year yield eased about 2bp to 4.154% and the 10-year about 2bp to 4.680%, with a September Fed hike now priced near 30%, down from roughly 50% a week earlier after soft retail sales and inflation data. Friday's megacap tape was dispersed rather than one-directional, with six of eight lower but Broadcom down 5.94% against AMD up 6.5% and Micron up 2.3%, leaving semiconductors slightly positive on average. Delayed cross-asset context shows Nasdaq futures firmer than the broader complex, VIX futures marginally bid, gold higher and Treasury futures modestly up - a conflicted rather than aligned configuration. Compressed index ranges, unaligned cross-assets, no Tier-1 US release scheduled today and no observed no-retracement path keep tail risk in the low band despite genuinely high stress. The principal structural checkpoint is the 13:30Z cash open, where opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would be the specific pattern capable of denying mean reversion; that structure is not observed in advance. FOMC minutes on 19 August at 18:00Z remain the week's main scheduled catalyst.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. Tail stayed in the low band throughout, ranging from 12 to 17, with the mapped policy state EA_ON for the entire window. Stress peaked at 82 during Saturday's US-hours window as Gulf war and crude headlines dominated, then eased into the high band around 67-70 overnight as the tape compressed. Dominant mode was mixed through the weekend session and settled to normal from 23:00Z as two-way overnight rotation established itself.
outlookSummary: The conditional path keeps tail in the low band across all 24 forecast hours, with the mapped policy state EA_ON throughout. Conditional risk sits at its lowest through the thin late-Asian and early European hours, rises gradually from the European cash open as real volume tests the narrow overnight band, and peaks at 18 across the 13:00Z-14:00Z window covering the US cash open, the opening auction and the NAHB release - the point at which opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would first become observable. It decays through the US afternoon, lifts again for the 19:00Z power hour where late-session continuation or reversal can be sharp, then returns to the overnight baseline after the 20:00Z cash close and holds there into Tuesday's Asian session. Stress stays in the high band throughout on the unresolved Gulf war and collapsed Hormuz traffic. Confidence decays with forecast distance because current price-path evidence cannot be extended reliably across a full day.
